name: terminal
description: Shell commands (foreground or background) with the working directory confined to accessible repositories. Background processes are managed with list/read/kill tools. With the sandbox on, a non-administrator's commands run inside a mount namespace holding only that account's own projects, so the shell respects the same boundary as the file tools. An administrator's shell is never confined.

configSchema.label: Isolation
configSchema.hint: How commands from non-administrator accounts are contained.

configSchema.label: Sandbox non-administrator commands
configSchema.hint: Run a non-administrator's shell commands inside a mount namespace containing only the projects assigned to that account, so the shell cannot read or write the rest of the machine. Privilege escalation is blocked as well: setuid binaries stop conferring rights, so sudo is refused. The toolchain, the network and the account's own projects stay fully available. An administrator's shell is never sandboxed. Requires bubblewrap on the host; without it a non-administrator's shell is refused rather than run unconfined.

configSchema.label: Limits
configSchema.hint: Output size and timeout caps for shell commands.

configSchema.label: Output cap
configSchema.hint: How many bytes of stdout/stderr are returned before truncation. Also caps the rolling output buffer kept for background processes.

configSchema.label: Command timeout (ms)
configSchema.hint: How long a foreground command may run before it is killed.

configSchema.label: Background processes per session
configSchema.hint: How many background processes one session may keep running at once; starting another is refused until one is killed. Range 1-64, default 16.
